acqinfo.head: Immediate Source of Acquisition
acqinfo.p: Ongoing collection of documents acquired by gift and purchase from various sources. Source information is recorded on each folder. For further information, consult the appropriate curator.

userestrict.head: Conditions Governing Use
userestrict.p: The General Collection Manuscript Miscellany is the physical property of the Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University. Literary rights, including copyright, belong to the authors or their legal heirs and assigns. For further information, consult the appropriate curator.

prefercite.head: Preferred Citation
prefercite.p: [Author], [Item Title]. General Collection Manuscript Miscellany. Beinecke Rare Book and Manuscript Library, Yale University.

accessrestrict.head: Conditions Governing Access
accessrestrict.p: The materials are open for research.
Restricted Fragile Papers may only be consulted with permission of the appropriate curator. Preservation photocopies for reference use have been substituted in the main files.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p: This finding aid is updated periodically to account for new materials that have been added to the Miscellany. The date of the most recent update is noted on the title page. For information on material that may have been incorporated into the Miscellany since the last update, please consult the Public Service Desk.

processinfo.head: Processing Information
processinfo.p:
Genet, Jean. Letter: Paris, to Juan Goytisolo, 1974 Nov 30, has been removed from this collection and filed with Jean Genet papers (GEN MSS 1739) in December 2024.
Wolf-Ferrari, Ermanno, 1876-1948 material has been recataloged and added GEN MSS MUSIC MISC.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: This finding aid encompasses single manuscripts and small groups of manuscripts acquired by the Beinecke Library from various sources and at various times, which the Library has chosen to describe here rather than as separate entries in Yale University Library's on-line Public Access Catalog (Orbis). These materials include literary and historical manuscripts, individual or small groups of letters, and single documents. Materials are grouped under headings for author or other personal or corporate name to which they most closely relate. Items of unidentified authorship are grouped under the heading "Unidentified" under the letter "U".

Items in this collection cataloged prior to 2021 were assigned group and item numbers (for example, Grp 115, Item F-1). This system was discontinued in 2021, with previously assigned group and item numbers retained as the folder number.

This list is ongoing, and it is subject to revision as new materials are acquired and, on occasion, as groups of manuscripts are removed and cataloged separately as artificial collections. When materials are removed and reclassified, a cross reference to the new call number is placed in the list. In addition to newly received items which have been described using current cataloging standards, this finding aid contains previously cataloged material. Descriptions for the latter items have been transcribed from card sets in the Manuscript Catalog; these entries are identified by "rec," followed by the year of the conversion, e.g., (rec/97).

Correspondence dating from 1922 concerns McKenney's efforts to create stuffed animals based on characters from Peter Rabbit. In the letter dated May 11, 1961, Burgess replies to McKenney's request for advice on short stories written for children.
Includes five envelopes.

did.unittitle: Letters : Egypt and Sicily, to Henri Peyre

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Autograph manuscript letters, signed, from Gide to Yale University professor Henri Peyre. Three of the letters, dated 1939, were written while Gide was traveling in Egypt, and concern Gide's work, the writing of Taha Hussein, and personal matters. The fourth letter, dated 1950, was written by Gide in Sicily, and he expresses regrets at his declining strength and inability to send Peyre a requested piece of writing. With envelopes. Accompanied by typescript transcriptions of the letters.

bioghist.head: Henry Hotchkiss (1801-1871)
bioghist.p: Henry Hotchkiss (1801-1871) was a New Haven investor and businessman. In 1843 Henry and his brother Lucius Hotchkiss became partners of the L. Candee Company, a rubber shoe manufacturer. By 1863, Henry was the President and Treasurer of the company as well as the President of the New Haven Country Bank and a trustee of the New Haven and New London Railroad.

"Reflexions presentees le 14 aout 1791 a Madame de Rosanbo"

persname.part: Le Peletier De Rosanbo, Louis, Marquis

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Poem by Le Peletier de Rosanbo and presumed to be in his hand.
In this birthday poem, the author draws a comparison between the happiness of himself and his wife and the unhappiness of the other Louis and Marie Antoinette, the King of France and his consort.
A manuscript note in an unidentified hand on the last page reads: "Vers de M. le Peletier de Rosanbo a Mme le Peletier de Rosanbo, sa femme, fille de Mr. de Malesherbes."
In French.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Notes and draft fragments for articles and books, holograph and typescript, corrected, some on verso of correspondence. Subjects include: human nature, the Renaissance, antiquity, Maurice Barrès and sport. Manuscript headings include: "Barcelone," "Chiens," "Football," "Jansénisme de M[lle] de C[oantré]," "Jeunesse," "Notes générale Tolstoï," "Pan," "Plaisir," "Poulain," "Religion" and "Rome." Also included are a table of contents for an unidentified work on bullfighting, notes for Port Royal, and a printed advertisement for Le Songe. There is correspondence from l'Association des écrivains combattants, l'Association des courriéristes littéraires des journaux quotidiens, Henry Bauchau, dated "8 Mars 1950," R[ené] Christian-Froge, Jacques-Napoléon Faure-Biquet, Bernard Grasset Éditeur, René Lacôte, Christian Mégret, R[owland?] Raven-Hart and others.
In French.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: AD written in an unidentified hand and signed by Abraham and Sarah Pierson and Phinehas and Jerusha Brainerd.
The quitclaim transfers ownership of land in Haddam, Killingworth, and Saybrook, left by Benjamin and Samuel Towner, to Daniel, Timothy, and Abraham Towner.
Also present are signatures of Mary Brainerd and Hezekiah Brainerd, justice of the peace, and an annotation dated Feb 24, 1762.
A reference to Abraham and Sarah Pierson, possibly the signers of this document, appears in a footnote in the Brainerd-Brainard Genealogy, v. II, part V, p. 44.

scopecontent.p: Two autograph manuscript letters, signed, sent while Ruff was stationed in the Aleutian Islands and other locations during his service in the United States Army. The letters discuss Ruff's daily life on base, including the opening of a library and his jobs as censor and personnel officer, and how much he misses the rare book room at Yale. One letter with envelope.

did.unittitle: Letters : to Walter de la Mare

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: 60 autograph manuscript letters, 12 autograph manuscript postcards, and four typescript letters, signed, from Sassoon to De la Mare. Sassoon discusses De la Mare's article about Robinson Crusoe and makes reference to authors, including Max Beerbohm, Robert Graves, Thomas Hardy, Ralph Hodgson, H. M. Tomlinson, and H. G. Wells. Some letters contain watercolor illustrations by Sassoon depicting unidentified men. Also includes two printed poems by Sassoon.

scopecontent.p: Eleven ALS and three fragments, two ALS and one TLS, from Whistler to Stephen Tennant discussing personal and literary matters, including Tennant's poetry, and mentioning Mary Coleridge, Siegfried Sassoon, [Thomas James?] Cobden-Sanderson, Christopher [Hassall], Charles Sumner, and others. With one draft AL from Tennant to Whistler and holograph drafts of two poems by Tennant, "Lusty Autumn" and one untitled poem on the verso of the letter dated "Sep 7th. 1969."
Includes five envelopes.

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Three autograph manuscript letters, signed, from Whistler to Siegfried Sasson discussing travel plans and personal matters. Also includes nine typescript copies of Whistler poems, including: "At Lengthening Range"; "Destinations"; "Flowers for Her Grave"; "No Answer"; "On the Skyline"; "Prayer at Ghostfade"; "The Shape of a Bird"; "What Music?"; and "Why Do They Call Us Away?".

did.unittitle: Papers relating to F. Max Mueller, and related materials

scopecontent.head: Scope and Contents
scopecontent.p: Letter to William Ireland Knapp, Mar 16, 1890; ANS to Addison Van Name, Mar 7, 1891, appended to a printed circular letter requesting contributions to a Testimonial Fund for Reinhold Rost, Feb, 1891; copy of a letter from Whitney to the editor of The Daily News, Mar 4, 1892, written in autograph manuscript in an unidentified hand, in reply to a letter attributed to Andrew Lang, Feb 19, [1892], with a clipping; and a copy of a letter to the editor of The Academy, written in autograph manuscript in an unidentified hand, Mar 19, 1892, with a clipping of "Professor Whitney's Reply to Max Mueller," Feb 14, 1876, from the Examiner.

Related materials are a copy of a letter from Reinhold Rost to the secretary to the delegates of the Clarendon Press, Mar 16, 1891, written in autograph manuscript in an unidentified hand, with a mimeographed copy of the letter; six ALS from Rost to Whitney, 1892, including a copy of portions of a letter from Mueller to Lord Cross; and a copy of a TL from A. Godley, to the secretary to the delegates of the Clarendon Press, May 13, 1891.
Also present is a fragment of a AM relating to Mueller, written in an unidentified hand, n.d.
